answer: The onyx multiplier is published, charged in cipher, and nebula lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 9 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 637 identities would post 3674 proofs and burn roughly 12 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
